transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

At nine years old, a washing machine is near or past its typical lifespan, so the repair may not be cost-effective. You should compare the estimated repair quote against the price of a new unit to decide if it is financially sensible. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drive belt [belt-driven machines ONLY]. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
I've turned it by hand with the power off and it turns freely and quietly, no scraping or rumbling. What would you suggest I look at next?

Check if the motor is receiving power when the cycle starts. If it has power but does not run, the motor or its capacitor may be faulty. Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?

I ran an empty spin-only cycle and the drum doesn't turn at all, same as in a normal wash. It fills and drains, but there's no spinning. I did notice a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, but not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
